result.title: What's in the box? Revealing Object Layouts Inside Opaque Boxes via Contactless Vibration Excitation and Sensing
result.summary: Can we reveal what is inside an opaque box by observing its surface vibrations? Objects inside a box alter its mechanical response, providing cues about their hidden locations. We introduce a method that uses these cues to predict a box's 2D occupancy layout entirely remotely. A nearby speaker excites vibrations, which we measure on one visible wall using a grid of laser points and a camera measuring each point's speckle-pattern shifts. Our model, WhisperBox, learns to encode these vibrations into a latent representation and decode it into an occupancy map of the box's contents. The method requires no physical contact to excite or sense vibrations. We demonstrate layout recovery across various boxes and single- and multiple-object scenes, with generalization to unseen object instances, positions, orientations, and weights, as well as changes in laser placement and excitation source. Our analysis reveals that informative frequency bands need not coincide with the box's resonances and that the learned latent space captures object placement and supports arithmetic operations. These results demonstrate the potential of remote vibration sensing to infer spatial layouts hidden from view.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 WhisperBox：用扬声器激发不透明箱体振动，以激光散斑网格和相机非接触测量可见壁面振动，学习将其编码为 latent 再解码为箱内物体的 2D 占据布局，并分析哪些频段携带信息、latent 是否保留位置信息及支持算术操作。
AI.relevance_reason: 从间接外部测量推断隐藏空间状态、并以解码探测 latent 是否保留位置信息，可能与 LVR 中「内部状态是否保留视觉细节、latent 内容可否被读出」的评估思路形成概念类比，可供核查，但领域相距较远、无直接方法迁移。
